item.title: Larry Rudolph Claimed His Wife Died in a Hunting Accident
item.description: Bianca Rudolph was fatally shot during a hunting trip in Zambia in 2016. Her husband Larry claimed it was an accident and collected nearly $4.9 million in life insurance. A federal jury convicted him of murder and mail fraud, and he was sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: Alexander Brothers Used Wealth to Lure Their Victims
item.description: Tal, Oren and Alon Alexander used wealth and status to exploit women for years. More than 70 women came forward, according to prosecutors. The brothers were convicted of federal sex trafficking offenses in March 2026 and each sentenced to 30 years in prison that October.

item.title: Egypt Covington Was Killed After Intruders Chose Her Home
item.description: Michigan singer Egypt Covington was killed in June 2017 after intruders entered her home while targeting her neighbor for a robbery. Her family pushed for a new investigation, and three men eventually pleaded guilty to second-degree murder in 2023.

item.title: Veronica Guerin Exposed Drug Gangs Despite Death Threats
item.description: Irish journalist Veronica Guerin continued investigating organised crime despite threats and violent attacks. Her murder in June 1996 prompted national outrage and helped drive changes in Ireland’s response to criminal gangs, including the creation of the Criminal Assets Bureau.
